subject: MAP: performance milestones & TTFT streaming run for Nimbus Health

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff + proposed perf evaluation plan (TTFT + streaming)

Samir —

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. As discussed, I attached a first draft MAP and a benchmarking plan focused on chat/text generation TTFT and streaming latency. Key asks from our side:

- Confirm the target workload profiles (avg concurrent users, typical prompt lengths, token budget per response).
- Agree on two benchmark windows:
  * Pilot: 1000 sessions, 2k messages, concurrency profile A (8 concurrent chat sessions)
  * Stress: 10k sessions, concurrency profile B (50 concurrent) for throughput SLOs
- Confirm acceptable SLOs and close timeline (we propose a pilot acceptance by 2027-05-22 and production pilot by 2027-05-29).

Benchmarking plan highlights (see attached bench-plan-streaming-v2.yaml):
- Measurements: TTFT (first-token time) and streaming p50/p95/p99, per-request throughput, successful token/sec, and KV-cache miss rate.
- Scenarios: cold-start (no cache), warmed prefix cache, and mixed production-like traffic.
- Tools: Redwood's streaming harness + client traces (we will provide an annotated trace file).

Deliverables during the MAP: map_v1 (milestones + acceptance criteria), raw CSV of runs, and a short executive one-pager with topline p50/p95/p99.

If this looks good I’ll schedule the pilot run for Friday (05/15) morning PT and will loop in our bench engineer.

Thanks,

Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the note and the drafts. Quick answers:

- Workload: our initial pilot should mirror the outpatient chat scenario — typical prompt lengths ~20-40 tokens, average response target ~150 tokens. Concurrency: pilot = 8 concurrent sessions (as you proposed).
- SLOs: we’re targeting TTFT p95 <= 250ms for streaming first-byte under normal load; p99 should be < 500ms ideally.
- Compliance: we need the bench harness to avoid persisting PHI. Can your traces be scrubbed?

Two requests before you run the pilot:
1) Can you share the exact client harness steps and a sample anonymized trace?
2) We’d like a quick runbook on how to reproduce the test on our side in case we want to validate.

Elena Ruiz (cc) will be the sign-off on the acceptance criteria.

Samir Patel

samir.p@nimbushealth.com

Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + proposed perf evaluation plan (TTFT + streaming)

Samir —

All good — thanks for clarifying. Short answers:

- Traces: yes, we will scrub traces to remove PHI fields. We’re attaching an anonymized sample trace and the bench YAML; they are descriptive only (no raw payloads).
- Repro runbook: attached to the MAP PDF and also posted to the shared Drive link below. Steps are:
  1) Provision test agent (we run from our dedicated infra to avoid egress issues)
  2) Run warmup: 500 sessions at low concurrency to populate prefix cache
  3) Pilot: 1k sessions, concurrency=8, record TTFT and streaming latency per token
  4) Stress: ramp to concurrency=50, measure throughput and p99 tail behavior

Pilot schedule: we’ll start Friday 2027-05-15 08:00 PT and expect ~4 hours for both pilot and a single stress pass. Deliverables by EOD Friday: raw CSV (bench-results-nimbus-v2.csv), annotated streaming trace (streaming-trace-20270515.json), and a two-page executive summary doc.

Acceptance targets we propose (for the MAP):
- TTFT p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 240ms, p99 <= 480ms under pilot concurrency (8).
- Streaming token p50/p95/p99 latencies measured at 20-token increments and end-to-end response completion times.

Let me know if you want us to tighten p99 further; we’ll also include notes on mitigations we’ll try during the stress run (prefix caching and adaptive batching).

Ava
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava@redwood.com

From: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 18:40:12 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Nimbus pilot results (raw + topline)

Team —

Quick internal recap before I push to the customer: we completed the pilot + one stress pass this morning. Attached are the raw CSV and the annotated streaming traces. Topline observations:

- Pilot (concurrency=8):
  * TTFT p50 = 48ms, p95 = 196ms, p99 = 422ms
  * Streaming per-token p50 = 12ms, p95 = 48ms, p99 = 120ms (measured at 20-token mark)
  * Success rate: 99.8%

- Stress pass (peak concurrency ~52):
  * Average throughput dropped ~18% vs linear due to KV-cache churn and larger batch timeouts.
  * TTFT p95 spiked to ~640ms for a small subset (~0.4%) of sessions where cache-miss + kernel recompile path hit.

Root cause hypothesis: the p99 tail in the stress run correlates with KV-cache eviction and occasional long-running memcpy on a particular GPU instance (we saw a handful of >700ms kernel latencies).

Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Enable prefix-level sticky routing for pilot tenants to keep hot KV on the same instance.
- Reduce max internal batch size from 64 -> 48 for the stress window to lower tail latency at the expense of ~4% throughput.
- Schedule a narrow canary with these changes and re-run the stress pass.

Next actions (I will):
1) Send a customer-facing summary + attachments (CSV + trace)
2) Propose the mitigations and schedule a canary for Monday 05/17
3) Ask for acceptance sign-off (Elena) to move to the production pilot by 05/29

Ava
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: bench-results-nimbus-v2.csv, streaming-trace-20270515.json

Ava / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed notes. Topline: these numbers are promising and within our appetite for the pilot. A few items before we call the pilot accepted:

- Please proceed with the mitigations you proposed and run the canary. We want a short canary (2 hours) to confirm p99 improves under a modest stress window.
- Please include a one-paragraph SLA note in the MAP about expected TTFT behavior and fallback routing if a region degrades.
- Confirm that all traces shared are scrubbed (no PHI).

If the canary looks good we can sign acceptance and move to production pilot stage targeted for 2027-05-29. Elena — if you agree I’ll sign off once we get the canary artifact.

Samir Patel
